blocking_findings.title: /courses publishes the banned discipline-acronym roster and a blanket unapproved CEC claim; the three new rules cannot see it
blocking_findings.summary: The catalogue page's FAQ renders the exact glossed IICRC discipline roster that the branch's new GLOSSED-LIST rule was written to kill on llms.txt, immediately followed by a course-level CEC claim, against an empty approvals registry. Both are invisible to the guard because the copy is interpolated through JSX elements and split across source lines.
blocking_findings.evidence: app/(public)/courses/page.tsx:288-299 renders: "CARSI offers IICRC CEC accredited courses across seven core disciplines: Water Restoration Technology (WRT), Carpet Repair and Reinstallation Technology (CRT), Applied Structural Drying (ASD), Applied Microbial Remediation Technology (AMRT), Fire and Smoke Restoration Technology (FSRT), Odour Control Technology (OCT), and Commercial Carpet Cleaning Technology (CCT). Eligible courses carry IICRC Continuing Education Credits (CECs) upon completion, with automatic tracking and verifiable digital credentials." src/components/ui/AcronymTooltip.tsx:46 renders `{children ?? term}` — the literal acronym reaches the DOM. Why the guard misses it: (a) the GLOSSED-LIST rule at scripts/check-iicrc-terminology.mjs:247 requires two literal `(<ACRONYM>)` tokens on ONE line, but in source each acronym sits inside `<AcronymTooltip term="WRT" />` with the closing paren on the NEXT line, and the CLI scans line-by-line (scripts/check-iicrc-terminology.mjs:530-533); (b) the CEC rule at line 109 requires `courses … carry … CEC(s)` within one line, but the source line ends at "Continuing Education" — `continuing[\s-]+education[\s-]+credits?` needs the word "Credits", which is on the following line. data/seed/cec-approvals.json holds `"approvals": []`. Verified undocumented: `grep -nEi "courses/page|catalogue page|seven core disciplines|AcronymTooltip|carry .*CEC|FAQ" BACKLOG.md DECISIONS.md GOAL.md docs/cec-submissions/DRAFT-COURSES-READINESS.md` returns one unrelated line (BACKLOG.md:147). Separately confirmed no OTHER in-scope file trips the three new rules: `git grep -nPi '\((WRT|RRT|ASD|AMRT|FSRT|CCT|CRT|OCT|TCST)\).*?\((WRT|…)\)'` hits only docs/audits/, docs/plans/ and the guard's own self-test (all out of scope), and the heading-form sweep `git grep -nPi '^ *#+ *(WRT|…)\b'` returns nothing repo-wide.
blocking_findings.failure_scenario: Merge and deploy. A learner or an AI crawler loads https://carsi.com.au/courses and reads CARSI's course range branded with seven IICRC Registered-Training-School discipline acronyms — the construction CLAUDE.md § 'CARSI designation rule' bans as licence-critical — plus 'Eligible courses carry IICRC Continuing Education Credits (CECs) upon completion' while data/seed/cec-approvals.json contains zero approvals. Meanwhile `npm run check:iicrc-terminology` and `npm run check:iicrc-compliance` both exit 0, and the branch's commit message and DRAFT-COURSES-READINESS.md read as though the branding sweep is complete. This is the same root cause the guard's own comment records for the /api/lms catch-all ('built by a template literal … so the acronym never appeared in source') — the branch fixed the arming and added three rules, but did not close the interpolation blind spot, and a live instance of it sits on the highest-traffic public page.
blocking_findings.required_action: Either rewrite the /courses FAQ answer to CARSI topic + designation framing (as public/llms.txt was), or record it as an explicit founder decision alongside DECISIONS #15/#16/#17 with a date. Whichever is chosen, the guard blind spot itself needs a recorded owner: a per-line regex cannot see JSX-interpolated copy, so either the scan needs a per-file (newline-tolerant) pass for these rules or a rendered-output check has to cover it. Both were verified by reading only — neither claim here was executed.

The `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" TERM=dumb` invocation required by the contract was constructed and denied (twice — once as a direct env -i call, once via a script that re-execs itself under env -i). No environment variable was exported at any point, so no evidence was poisoned; there simply is no evidence.

Direct callers examined for every changed contract. resolveCheckoutRedirect: all six call sites read in the diff; each passes `request.nextUrl.origin` (URL/Host-derived), never `request.headers.get('origin')`. Verified for all six, including the two whose `origin` binding sits ABOVE the diff hunk: `grep -n "origin" app/api/lms/checkout/route.ts` shows line 61 `const origin = request.nextUrl.origin;`, and app/api/lms/onboarding/[slug]/checkout/route.ts binds it in-hunk. This mattered because a browser sets the Origin header automatically on cross-site fetch, which would have made the allowlist attacker-controlled. Since the fallback defaults are built from the same origin, admitting it concedes nothing new, as the module docstring states. resolveResponseStatus: sole caller is fetchApi in the same file (line ~156); effects on the 401-refresh branch and on transient 503s recorded as P2-3. cloudinaryDeliveryUrl: sole caller is CourseTextThumbnail.tsx:190; CourseThumbnail.tsx was checked and only gained a comment, so no double-wrap — and the helper is idempotent by construction anyway (second pass sees `f_auto` as the first segment and returns unchanged). resolveDisciplineTab: exported from CourseGrid and consumed via `initialTab` at app/(public)/courses/page.tsx:211, which upper-cases the query value at line 125 — confirming the fix is real and that deep links previously always fell back to 'All'. I then checked that the newly-working filter is not empty for the three tabs the changed CTAs now point at: `grep -oiE '"category": "[^"]*"' data/seed/courses-catalog.json | sort | uniq -c` shows 'Water Damage Restoration' (16), 'Mould Remediation' (1), 'Cleaning'/'Commercial Cleaning' (2), and 40 title/category rows match 'cleaning' — so no CTA now lands on an empty catalogue. classifyCheckoutProbe: called once in the same file and by the new self-test. inScope: exported and now also consumed by check-iicrc-terminology.test.mjs.

Nothing in the diff creates an account, sends a message, publishes, purchases or pushes. The two new pages contain no network calls: `grep -nE 'fetch\(|sendMail|resend|nodemailer|axios|process.env|mailto:|stripe\.' app/(public)/refund-policy/page.tsx app/(public)/support/page.tsx` returns nothing. docs/cec-submissions/COVER-EMAIL.md is a draft for the founder to send by hand; nothing in the repo references or transmits it, and each pack ends with 'Registry status for this course: not_submitted'. scripts/verify-go-live-readiness.mjs performs outbound HTTP but is read-only GET/POST probes against the site's own BASE_URL, and this diff makes it strictly safer by adding the isCli guard so importing the module no longer fires the probes. The six checkout routes still call Stripe, but the diff narrows what they may pass, never widens it. The e2e purchase spec deliberately stops short of a real payment and says so.
